one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the window: Q3 2026 results and call on 2026-10-20 after the close [2]. Consensus is about $2.64 non-GAAP EPS on about $2.91B revenue [5]. A Barchart/Yahoo preview quoting $2.13 uses stale 2025-era figures and I ignored it. Management guided full-year da Vinci procedure growth near the 14.5% midpoint [1][19], which implies H2 growth of roughly 13-14%. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $2.80 beat by about $0.30 [1][19], and Intuitive has beaten for four straight quarters, so an EPS beat is likely. What will move the stock is three other things. (1) U.S. procedure growth: it was 12% in Q2, and hospital-level data shows the softest elective-surgery environment outside COVID (Community Health Systems inpatient surgeries -3.8% in Q2 [26], ACA enrollment -12-13% [26][27]). U.S. growth of 11-12% is my base case and is roughly expected. (2) The first quantification of the Extended Use Program (H1 2027 launch, lowers instrument revenue per procedure in high-volume benign cases), which management promised for this call [19]. This is a real negative-skew risk to 2027 numbers. (3) Early Ottava commentary, probably benign given J&J's selective, capacity-limited launch [24][25]. The stock already rebounded about 15% from about $350-365 in mid-September (insider 10b5-1 sale prints) to $414.55 on 2026-09-28 after the SP CE mark [21], so the post-Q2 washout is partly reversed. Net: median about $400 (flat). Sigma is about 11-12% for the month, above the 37%/3.5 = 10.6% baseline because the earnings gap is inside the window (ISRG moved 10-15% on recent prints). I gave the tails a slight negative skew for the EUP quantification.

fair_value.method: Three-method blend. Forward P/E: FY2028 non-GAAP EPS of about $13.6 x 31 = $422 (weight 0.5). EV/sales: 2028 consensus revenue of $14.96B x 9.5x plus about $9.5B net cash, over 355M shares = $427 (weight 0.25). FCF yield: 2028 FCF of about $5.24B at a 3.7% EV yield plus net cash = $426 (weight 0.25). Blended fair value 12 months out is about $424, about 6% above the $401.24 close.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (~FY2028 non-GAAP) $13.6 x 31x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Re-checked on StockAnalysis 2026-10-01; consistent with H1 run-rate (Q2 $2.80 [1]) plus Q3 consensus $2.64.
StockAnalysis 2026-10-01 shows $12.09 (+12.2%) [5], confirming the earlier Yahoo figure [6].

MarketScreener GAAP consensus grows 14.7% in 2028 ($10.66 to $12.23) [20]. Applied to the $12.09 non-GAAP 2027 consensus [5], that gives $13.87, which matches my round-1 $13.9 estimate. I take a 2% haircut for the Extended Use Program (H1 2027, not yet quantified, not likely fully in consensus) [19] and 2027 Medicaid work-requirement coverage losses [26]: $13.6.

Stock is at about 34x NTM non-GAAP EPS now ($401 / about $11.8 blended FY26-27 [5]) and about 33x per [4]. It was 48-55x a year ago [12][16], and the P/E fell from the high-70s to 38x on GAAP [17]. I take about 3 turns off for EPS growth slowing to about 13-15% and a full year of Ottava/Hugo marketing. I do not cut further because J&J's Ottava production capacity is limited through 2027 [25] and about 85% of revenue is recurring [12].

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2028 consensus revenue $14.96B x 9.5x EV/NTM sales + ~$9.5B net cash at Sep-2027, /355M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener consensus: 2026 $11.76B, 2027 $13.26B, 2028 $14.96B. This replaces my round-1 estimate of $15.2B.
Consensus EV/sales is 11.7x on 2026 and 10.0x on 2027 [20]. I trim about 0.5x for slower growth and the EUP's effect on instrument pricing [19].
$8.63B at 6/30/26 with no debt [1]. Consensus net cash is $6.57B at end-2026 and $10.48B at end-2027 [20], so about three-quarters of the way through 2027 gives about $9.5B.
357.3M in Q2 2026, with about 0.9M bought back per quarter [1], gives about 355M by Q3 2027 net of dilution.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2028 FCF ~$5.24B / 3.7% EV FCF yield = $141.6B EV + $9.5B net cash, /355M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener consensus 2028 FCF of $5.345B [20], less 2% for EUP risk [19].

Today: 2027 consensus FCF of $4.72B [20] over about $135B EV ($143B market cap [4] less $8.6B cash) gives 3.5% NTM. The trailing cash yield is about 2.7% [17]. I assume slight further de-rating to 3.7%.

bear.story: Several things go wrong together. U.S. procedure growth slides to about 9-10% as ACA coverage losses carry into the 2027 Medicaid work requirements [26][27] and bariatric volumes keep falling [28]. The EUP cuts instrument revenue per procedure by more than feared [19], and remanufactured Xi instruments gain share [29]. Ottava wins early cholecystectomy/hernia accounts and China share erodes to domestic robots priced 60-75% lower [30][31]. Result: FY2028 EPS of about $12.5 at about 23x.

base.story: Procedure growth settles at 12-14%. The dV5 upgrade cycle (246 of 468 Q2 placements [1]), Ion (+36% [1]) and SP indications (CE mark for transvaginal gyn [21]) keep revenue growing about 13% [20]. The EUP takes about 1-2% off 2027-28 EPS. Ottava's ramp is capacity-limited [25]. FY2028 EPS of about $13.6-13.9 at about 31x.

bull.story: U.S. growth proves resilient: it held 12% while hospital surgeries fell [26], a sign of strong share gain from laparoscopy. The EUP expands ASC/international volume enough to offset the price cut. Ottava and Hugo stay niche through 2027 [22][25]. EPS of about $14.5 and the multiple re-rates toward 38x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $300 (8% under the $328.57 52-week low, about 22x my FY2028 EPS and roughly 25x the FY2027 consensus), the market would be pricing a structural break rather than sentiment. That would mean U.S. da Vinci procedure growth in single digits, an EUP and remanufacturing hit that shrinks instruments-and-accessories revenue per procedure by high single digits, or visible share loss to Ottava/Hugo in benign general surgery. The 12-14% grower with a recurring-revenue moat would no longer be the right model.

key_uncertainties: Size of the Extended Use Program hit to instrument revenue per procedure from H1 2027. Management deferred quantification to the Q3 call [19].

Whether the U.S. slowdown (14% to 12%) is cyclical or persists. ACA coverage losses fed almost entirely into the uninsured, and 2027 Medicaid work requirements add a second leg [26][27]. GLP-1s keep shrinking bariatrics [28].
Speed of Ottava adoption in benign general surgery. J&J gives no placement targets and production is constrained through 2027 [24][25], but surgeons at SRS rated it the best-positioned challenger.
China share loss to domestic robots priced 60-75% below da Vinci [30][31]. The Toumai share claim is single-sourced.
Remanufactured Xi instruments. Restore Robotics now has several FDA clearances and Intuitive will not void service contracts [29]. The scale of adoption is unverified.
Multiple path: already about 34x from about 50x. Bull and bear cases are both mostly a multiple question.
reasoning: Continuation of round 1, which ran out of search budget after about 15 queries. I ran about 30 more searches and fetches. Verified facts: Q2 2026 revenue $2.89B (+19%), da Vinci procedures +15% (U.S. +12%), Ion +36%, 468 placements including 246 dV5, non-GAAP EPS $2.80 vs $2.19, cash $8.63B, 357.3M diluted shares [1]. Gross margin guide raised to 68-69% [19]. Consensus FY26/FY27 non-GAAP EPS of $10.78/$12.09 [5], and MarketScreener's 2026-28 revenue, GAAP EPS and FCF path [20] confirm my round-1 FY2028 EPS of about $13.9 and lower 2028 revenue slightly to $14.96B. New bear evidence I could not chase in round 1: (a) an Extended Use Program from H1 2027 will lower instrument revenue per procedure, size not disclosed [19]; (b) hospital-level data shows the ACA subsidy cliff pushed patients almost entirely into the uninsured, with elective surgeries falling at HCA/CHS, and Medicaid work requirements start in 2027 [26][27]. That undercuts my round-1 bull assumption that the headwinds simply lap in 2027. (c) Remanufactured Xi instruments now have multiple 510(k)s [29]; (d) domestic Chinese robots priced 60-75% below da Vinci [31] and reportedly ahead in China share [30]. New bull and mitigating evidence: Ottava's ramp is capacity-limited through 2027 and J&J frames it as material only by decade-end [24][25]. A long-time robotics practitioner flags real workflow limits of the table-mounted design [22][23]. ISRG grew U.S. procedures 12% while hospital surgeries fell, which implies continued share gain from open and laparoscopic surgery. The CE mark for SP transvaginal gyn lifted the stock 6.5% [21]. Hiring is still expanding (682-717 postings, +25-28% over 3 months, weighted to sales and autonomy [14]). Independent September newsletters are constructive but cautious: TIKR models about $585 by 2030 at a $369 price [18]; LASER bought at $480 and calls the entry premature but sees 15-20% FCF/share growth [17]; Jimmy's Journal estimates 70-80% soft-tissue share [16]. Insider sales in September were small and under 10b5-1 plans. No Reddit or X material worth citing (X not reachable), and no prediction market on ISRG, Ottava or Hugo. Twelve Data estimates were behind a plan wall. Valuation: P/E $422, EV/sales $427, FCF yield $426, blended to $424 (vs $431 in round 1, lower on the EUP/Medicaid haircut and the lower revenue consensus). Scenarios $290/$428/$560 at 25/50/25 give a mean of about $427. Ladder: a mixture of lognormals (70% sigma 0.28, 30% sigma 0.45) around a $408 median, giving a mean of about $432 and an effective sigma of about 0.33. That is slightly below the 37% realized vol, which includes the one-off Ottava/guidance repricing, but with fat tails for the competitive and EUP binaries. P(>=401) = 0.52, down from 0.56. The consensus target of about $476-482 [5] sits near my 63rd percentile. I treat it as lagging evidence, not the answer.
